transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-02 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~61 minutes
- Redwood: Maya Chen (AE), Omar Vasquez (SE)
- Clearwater Bio: James Patel (CTO), Lena Hoffman (Head of ML), Arjun Rao (Infra Eng)

Summary:
Quick kickoff for onboarding Clearwater Bio onto Redwood's hosted/dedicated hybrid plan. Cover runtime intake, network/VPC requirements, pilot scope, security artifacts, and next steps to get a pilot running mid-May. Some audio stutter in a few spots; speaker labels mixed at times.

Topics covered:
- Goals for pilot and success criteria
- Network/VPC and egress/firewall expectations
- Data residency and KMS requirements
- Baseline perf/latency runs and benchmark strategy
- Access/SSO and role mapping for Console

Action items (high level): see metadata action_items above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll give a quick intro then jump into runtime and network. Maya here, I'm the AE. Omar is our systems engineer who'll drive the technical checklist.
[00:18] James Patel: Thanks Maya. Quick context — we're a mid-stage bioinformatics company, starting to surface LLM features in our curation pipeline. Timeline is tight, hoping a pilot within two weeks.
[00:30] Omar Vasquez: Awesome. Two-week pilot is doable; goal today is to capture the blockers — networking, security, and a minimal perf baseline. Also, do you expect to run on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated?
[00:45] Lena Hoffman: We want to start hosted to iterate quickly, but long term probably dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation. Also looking at on-prem for some PII workflows later.
[01:05] James Patel: Yes, hosted for pilot, dedicated for production. Key constraints: strict egress rules, our data team wants KMS integration, and we need audit logs for the evaluators.
[01:20] Omar Vasquez: Noted. We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and can emit audit logs per request, we'll share the format. Also we can offer a private control plane for the Private deployment later.
[01:40] Arjun Rao: On networking, we'll likely have a corporate VPC with limited egress. Do you allow peering, or do we need to open specific outbound IP ranges?
[01:55] Maya Chen: Good question. For hosted, we provide static egress IPs for enterprise tiers, and for Dedicated/Private you can either peer or use a private endpoint. We'll share the list of egress IP ranges and the peering doc.
[02:15] Lena Hoffman: Perfect. Also for the model, will you host our fine-tuned weights or do we need to provide a container?
[02:28] Omar Vasquez: We can do both. For pilot, easiest is to upload a model artifact to our catalog; for stricter air-gapped environments we support bringing your own container or on-prem package. There's a small mapping mismatch: sometimes our auto transcribe shows 'model artifact upload' as 'model artifactual' — sorry that's the transcript, not the product.
[02:50] James Patel: Haha, okay. Regarding perf, we need 95th perc latency under 300ms for small counseling prompts — is that realistic?
[03:05] Omar Vasquez: Depends on model size/sequence length and batch settings. For a 7B quantized model under a dedicated GPU pool, 300ms 95p is achievable for short sequences; hosted varies by load. We'll propose a baseline config and a perf runbook.
[03:30] Maya Chen: We'll include recommended batching and KV cache options in the runbook. For the pilot, can you send a representative prompt set, Lena?
[03:45] Lena Hoffman: Yes — I'll share three prompt families and a simple evaluation rubric.
[03:52] (brief crosstalk)
[04:05] Omar Vasquez: On auth, we support SAML SSO and role-based access control. For your infra team, we'll map roles: infra admins, app devs, and read-only auditors. Any special SSO provider you're using?
[04:20] Arjun Rao: Okta.
[04:23] Omar Vasquez: Great, standard. We'll send the SAML metadata and a short setup doc.
[04:36] (pause)
[05:00] James Patel: About data residency — some of our datasets are EU-only, but most inference happens in US. Can you pin model endpoints to regions?
[05:12] Maya Chen: Yes, routing policies allow region pinning per route and per-customer. For mixed residency you can set a policy to keep EU data in EU regions; we'll share the region capabilities doc.
[05:30] Lena Hoffman: Also interested in how Redwood handles model rollouts and fallback — we want automatic fallback to smaller models under load.
[05:45] Omar Vasquez: We have a rollout system: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to compatible variants. We'll add an example config for fallback to 4-bit quantized variants with a lower token budget.
[06:00] Arjun Rao: For monitoring, we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the console, plus tracing hooks to our internal observability. Integrations?
[06:12] Omar Vasquez: Console provides per-route metrics and token breakdown. We also support tracing exports via OpenTelemetry to your collector. We'll include a sample dashboard and a JSON schema for logs.
[06:30] James Patel: Security pack — can you send SOC2 summary, encryption notes, and retention options?
[06:38] Maya Chen: Yes, security pack will be in the shared drive link. We'll include retention controls and transcript redaction options.
[06:50] (sound of a dog barking faintly in background, transcript note)
[07:05] Lena Hoffman: One more question: what's the onboarding support cadence? Will we have direct Slack to a CS engineer?
[07:15] Maya Chen: Yes, pilot customers get a dedicated CSM channel and weekly check-ins. For tech escalations Omar will be the primary SE.
[07:28] James Patel: Great. For the pilot success criteria — we want: stable infra for 50 concurrent requests, 95p latency under 300ms on our canonical prompts, and quality metrics above threshold per Lena's rubric.
[07:45] Omar Vasquez: Understood. We'll codify those into the runbook and measurement plan.
[08:00] Maya Chen: Ok real quick I'll read back next steps and owners. Maya will share the staging guide and onboarding checklist. Omar will produce the perf baseline runbook and sample container/imagenotes. Arjun will give us the VPC CIDR and egress rules. Lena will share prompt sets and evals.
[08:18] James Patel: Confirming pilot target window — we'd like to start 2026-05-18 and run two weeks. Any objections?
[08:25] Omar Vasquez: That lines up — we'll aim to have the staging environment ready and baseline runs available by 2026-05-11 so you can review.
[08:40] Lena Hoffman: Sounds good. Also, if we bump into network policy delays, can we use a short-lived token-based proxy for the pilot?
[08:50] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide a short-term tunnel/proxy for onboarding phases; we'll document the steps.
[09:05] (some overlapping talk)
[09:25] Omar Vasquez: One technical note — for prefix caching and KV cache settings, if your prompts have repeated context we can dramatically reduce token costs; include a note in the prompt sets.
[09:40] Lena Hoffman: We will.
[09:45] James Patel: Any competitors we should be aware of? We've been evaluating Anthropic and Bedrock for hosting — main tie-breakers are cost predictability and deployment flexibility.
[09:58] Maya Chen: Totally. We'll include a short comparison deck highlighting dedicated pools, model quantization and predictable unit economics.
[10:12] Arjun Rao: For SSO and audit trails, how long do you retain logs by default?
[10:20] Omar Vasquez: Default 90 days but enterprise retention is configurable; we can support 1-year retention for audit logs on request.
[10:35] (brief silence)
[10:50] Maya Chen: Ok let's capture the concrete next steps again — I'll upload the staging doc to the shared link: https://redwood.example/share/clearwater-onboard. Omar will attach the perf runbook and example OpenTelemetry pipeline.
[11:10] Lena Hoffman: I'll send the prompt families and rubric after the call.
[11:15] James Patel: Arjun will send the networking constraints and CIDRs by EOD Tuesday.
[11:22] Maya Chen: Great. Any final Qs?
[11:28] (murmurs)
[11:40] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar items for the network walkthrough and the SAML setup.
[11:50] (meeting ends)
